spec: Build a contact-form backend. Visitors submit messages with a name, email and message body; administrators can list all messages and delete individual ones. Messages are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Single message store with create, list, and delete operations.

congruence_checklist: Message model has name, email, body

plan.summary: A JSON REST API that accepts public contact-form submissions (name, email, message) and stores them in DynamoDB, plus admin-only endpoints to list, retrieve and delete stored messages. The service runs as a standalone FastAPI process that talks directly to DynamoDB, using an admin API key held in Secrets Manager and emitting operational logs to CloudWatch.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe used by the evaluation harness; reports service status and DynamoDB table reachability.
Public endpoint: accept a contact-form submission (name, email, message), validate it, assign an id and timestamp, and persist it to the DynamoDB messages table.
Admin endpoint: list all stored contact messages with optional pagination (limit / next_token) and newest-first ordering.
Admin endpoint: retrieve a single contact message by its id; 404 when it does not exist.
Admin endpoint: delete a single contact message by its id; 404 when it does not exist.

data_models.name: ContactMessage
fields: source_ip: str | None (client IP captured at submission)

aws_resources.name: contact-form-messages
aws_resources.justification: Primary datastore explicitly required by the spec: stores each submitted contact message. Partition key message_id (S); the app puts items on POST /messages, scans/queries on GET /messages, gets on GET /messages/{id} and deletes on DELETE /messages/{id}.

aws_resources.name: contact-form/admin-api-key
aws_resources.justification: The spec separates public submitters from administrators, so the admin list/delete endpoints need a credential. The application reads this secret at startup to validate the X-Admin-API-Key header.

aws_resources.name: contact-form-backend-app-role
aws_resources.justification: Least-privilege role/policy granting the standalone backend PutItem/GetItem/Scan/DeleteItem on the messages table, GetSecretValue on the admin API key secret, and CloudWatch Logs write access.

aws_resources.name: /contact-form/backend
aws_resources.justification: Log group the application writes request and error logs to, providing operational visibility for submissions and admin deletions.

events: 🧭 Parsed specification → contact_form_backend (fastapi); AWS resources: DynamoDB:contact-form-messages, Secrets Manager:contact-form/admin-api-key, IAM:contact-form-backend-app-role, CloudWatch:/contact-form/backend

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 6 files — FastAPI contact-form backend split into `app.py` (routes, pydantic models, admin API-key auth via env var or Secrets Manager, error handlers) and `storage.py` (a `MessageRepository` interface with DynamoDB and in-memory implementations, opaque base64 pagination cursors, boto3 clients honouring `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` and default region `us-east-1`). Endpoints: `GET /health`, public `POST /messages` (validated name/email/message, UUID id, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, source IP), and admin-guarded `GET /messages` (limit/next_token, newest first), `GET /messages/{id}`, `DELETE /messages/{id}` with 404s. Email validation uses a stdlib regex so no extra packages are needed. Tests use `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` with dependency-overridden in-memory repo plus a fake DynamoDB table stub, covering every endpoint, auth failures, pagination, storage errors and secret resolution — all offline. Only flask/fastapi/uvicorn/boto3/pydantic-family deps; no debug flags, eval, shell, or hardcoded credentials.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the contact-form backend, one-to-one with the plan's aws_resources: a DynamoDB table `contact-form-messages` (partition key `message_id`, PAY_PER_REQUEST, point-in-time recovery, SSE with a customer managed KMS key), a Secrets Manager secret `contact-form/admin-api-key` (KMS-encrypted, seeded with a generated 40-char key via hashicorp/random), a CloudWatch log group `/contact-form/backend` (365-day retention, KMS-encrypted), and a least-privilege IAM role `contact-form-backend-app-role` with a policy scoped to exactly that table ARN, that secret ARN, that log group ARN/streams and the CMK — no wildcard actions or resources. A single CMK (rotation enabled, scoped key policy allowing only the account root and the regional CloudWatch Logs service principal) satisfies the Checkov CMK-encryption checks for DynamoDB, Secrets Manager and CloudWatch. Files: `versions.tf` (terraform block pinning hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 and hashicorp/random ~> 3.5), `main.tf` (provider with project/managed-by/environment default_tags plus all resources), `variables.tf` (defaults matching the plan's resource names), `outputs.tf` (table, secret, log group, role and key identifiers for the app). Only LocalStack Community services are used — no Lambda, RDS, ECS, EKS or ElastiCache. The only Checkov suppression is an inline, justified skip of CKV2_AWS_57 (automatic secret rotation would require a rotation Lambda outside the plan's scope).
